Name: Kanwalpal Singh Flora
Question: Do Indian Punjabis eat Punjabi food like butter masala and tandoori chicken at home every day?
Answer: Not at all. I have read that these creamy/tandoori type Punjabi food actually has influence from Persian/Afghani type of food(aka Mughlai), which todays ‘Indian Punjabis’ brought with them from the Western side of Punjab/NWFP post partition. They did change the base ingredients and added more masala/spice to the local liking.[1] You will mostly find these types of food in Punjabi restaurants and functions/weddings etc. My Mother is from the Eastern side of Punjab and is actually vegetarian, so 90–95% of our home food is also vegetarian. 5% is meat based as my Dad grew up in the Northeast, and that also mostly in the last few years as he developed an interest in making food. I also have lived a few years in rural Punjab(both Doaba and Malwa) and meat is rarely made at home. People get shocked when they see Punjabi meat eating percentage at the level of Gujarat and Rajasthan, but it will be clear to anyone who has spent some time in rural Punjab that it is true. Regular Indian Punjabi home food is thus very plain Dals(Lentils), Allo Gobhi, Rajma, Kadhi, Chote and Wadde Chole, Various types of Saags, Matar Paneer, Allo Paronthe and so on. So, we come to this weird conundrum that what is widely perceived as ‘Punjabi Food’ worldwide is not really eaten on a regular basis by Punjabis(Indian) themselves. Many Indian restaurants here in the US actually are Punjabi, and I explain the same thing to my colleagues that we don’t really eat this food every day at home. I am not saying we don’t enjoy it, just that we eat all these types of tandoori/creamy food sparsely. Once in a while, you run into a Punjabi family, where the host is a real food connoisseur and has an interest in making foods like these at home, but that is so unlikely that one remembers each instance. In Summary we can probably divide Indian Punjabi food in 3 types, first is the normal plain home food, next is some type of creamy/tandoori food(but vegetarian only, this is called Vaishno Food in Punjab, ie Dal Makhani, Shahi Paneer etc which can be found all over Indian Punjab markets), third is the one mentioned in the question. (Butter Chicken, Tandoori Chicken etc).

Question: What does the Punjabi word "shae" mean? I've heard it many times before in different sentences like "Tinu kon shae dinda?" Or "prawa ena lokan nu shae lab jandi aah thora jeya has k Gaal kr lawao tae!"
Answer: The word is ਸ਼ਹਿ/شہِ. Shahi Though it’s pronounced more like ਸ਼ੈ/شے (The way you have written, Shae). This is because of the Tonal nature of ਹ/H/ہ in Punjabi. The meaning of the word is ‘incitement, instigation or power behind a crime’. prawa ena lokan nu shae lab jandi aah thora jeya has k Gaal kr lawao tae : Brother, these people find ‘power to instigate’, if we just talk to them in a friendly manner. Now Ofcourse, interestingly, there is another word , Shae ਸ਼ੈ/شے which means ‘Thing’ as in ‘Cheez’. Tu Kehdi Waddi Shae A What do you think of yourself/ who do you think you are. So, that is why Punjabi is called a Tonal Language.

Question: What is the meaning of the Punjabi word “toye”?
Answer: Toya or To-aa ਟੋਆ means a pit , a cavity or hole in ground both natural or man made. Toye is plural of the same. (or when reffering to it). It is also used for Dimples of Human Face. Oh Toye Che Digh Gaya Si (He had fallen in the pit). Gallan De Toye. (Dimples of the cheeks).

Question: What is corner in Punjabi?
Answer: While ‘Kona/KoNa’ is used in Punjabi (from Sanskrit), another Punjabi word for Corner is ‘Khunja’, ਖੂੰਜਾ. Main Unhu Khunje Laata. (I put him to the corner/side). This is of figure of speech use, saying you ‘took care’ of someone, as in if you are in competition with someone. Khunje Che Pya Hona (It must be at the corner). Or the following line I found online. ਚਾਰੇ ਖੂੰਜੇ ਹਿੱਲੇ ਬਾਬਲ ਨੇ ਧੀ ਤੋਰੀ : Chare Khunje Hille Baabal Ne Dhi Tori. All four corners shook when Father let his Daughter go. (Post Marriage).
